name: AI Security Tooling
blurb: The defensive tooling landscape, organized by six security domains: Security Governance and Risk Management, Security Operations, Architecture and Engineering, Application and Product Security, Third-Party and Supply Chain Risk, and Data Protection and Privacy.

items.name: Security Governance and Risk Management
items.note: Continuous compliance monitoring, AI risk registers, policy engines, and audit-evidence automation - the governance layer of the defensive stack.

items.name: Security Operations
items.note: AI-assisted detection, triage, and investigation; agent behavioral analytics; supervision and kill-switch controls for autonomous response.

items.name: Architecture and Engineering
items.note: Model gateways, prompt firewalls, inference-time guardrails, and the network and identity architecture around AI workloads.

items.name: Application and Product Security
items.note: LLM application scanning, red-team automation, evaluation harnesses, and secure development guardrails for AI features.

items.name: Third-Party and Supply Chain Risk
items.note: Model and dataset provenance, AI bills of materials, registry scanning, and vendor AI monitoring.

items.name: Data Protection and Privacy
items.note: Semantic data loss prevention, discovery and classification for training corpora, purpose enforcement, and erasure tooling.

items.name: Where the categories come from
items.note: OWASP's GenAI Security Project maintains the open threat and solutions landscape these categories draw on; patterns, not product picks.
